userStories.title: Resolve profile contestants
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve every `--compare` value as a profile and build the profile-derived contestant configuration.

**Motivation** — Comparing agent names is also the wrong axis. A profile already bundles agent, per-tier models, and arbitrary config overrides — which is what a comparison wants to vary.

**Approach** — Contestants are **profile names**. `--compare cross-agent-pi,cross-agent-mm` resolves each name through the existing asynchronous profile loader with the bake-off project root and deep-merges its overlay onto the base config, the same layering `src/config/loader.ts` applies for `--profile`.

Accepting *either* an agent name or a profile name was rejected: profile names already collide with agent names (`~/.nax/profiles/opencode.json` and `.nax/profiles/codex.json` both exist), so any disambiguation rule silently produces a different comparison than intended. A separate `--compare-profiles` flag was rejected as two flags for one concept.

The existing field names are **retained**: `BakeoffOptions.agents` and `ContestantResult.agent` keep their names and carry profile names as their values. Renaming them would ripple through `types.ts`, ranking, report rendering and six test files for no functional gain, and `run-action.test.ts` asserts on `callArg.agents` today.

**Scope** — In: profile loading, unknown-profile validation, resolved-agent ACP/PATH validation, deep merge, and fallback pinning. Out: per-contestant worktrees/output contexts (US-002); runner adapter (US-003); branch and PRD guards (US-004); accepting bare agent names as contestants; `--compare` accepts profile names only.
acceptanceCriteria: When `validateContestants` resolves profile `cross-agent-pi`, then it returns `validAgents` containing `cross-agent-pi` and an empty `errors` array.
When a named profile does not resolve, then `validateContestants` returns one error with reason `unknown-profile`.
When one profile is unresolvable and another resolves in the same `validateContestants` call, then `validAgents` omits the unresolvable profile and retains the resolvable profile.
When `validateContestants` rejects an unresolvable profile, then its error message contains that profile name.
When `validateContestants` processes contestant names, then it invokes `loadProfile` once per name with that name as the first argument.
When a resolved profile's `agent.default` is absent from the ACP adapter registry, then `validateContestants` returns reason `no-acp-adapter`.
When a resolved profile's agent binary is absent from PATH, then `validateContestants` returns reason `dnf-not-installed`.
When a profile overlay exclusively sets a configuration key, then the contestant merged config returns the profile value for that key.
When both base config and a profile overlay set a configuration key, then the contestant merged config returns the profile value for that key.
When a contestant config is merged from a profile, then its `agent.default` equals the profile's `agent.default`.
When a profile overlay sets `agent.fallback.enabled` to true, then the contestant merged config has `agent.fallback.enabled` equal to false.

routing.reasoning: Changes profile resolution semantics across config and bake-off validation while preserving compatibility field names.

modifiedFiles.reason: asserts `result.errors[0].reason` is `"unknown-agent"` for a name absent from `KNOWN_AGENT_NAMES`, and that `validateContestants(["claude","codex"])` yields those names in `validAgents`. Contestants are profiles under this story, so both assertions pin a resolution path that no longer exists. US-001 owns replacing them with the profile equivalents: an unresolvable profile yields reason `"unknown-profile"`, and a resolvable profile name appears in `validAgents`.

userStories.title: Provide isolated contestant execution contexts
acceptanceCriteria: When `runContestant` invokes its pipeline dependency, then the context `profile` equals the contestant profile name.
When `runContestant` invokes its pipeline dependency, then the context `feature` equals the bake-off feature.
When `runContestant` invokes its pipeline dependency, then the context `worktree` path ends with the contestant worktree ID.
When a bake-off runs two contestants, then their pipeline contexts have different `worktree` values.
When `runContestant` invokes its pipeline dependency, then the context `outputDir` equals the project output root joined with `bakeoff`, the feature, and the profile name.
When a bake-off runs two contestants, then their pipeline contexts have different `outputDir` values.
When `runContestant` invokes its pipeline dependency, then `context.config.outputDir` equals `context.outputDir`.
When the pipeline dependency rejects, then `runContestant` returns status `dnf-crashed`.
When the first contestant pipeline rejects in a bake-off, then the coordinator still invokes the pipeline for the second contestant.
When a two-contestant bake-off completes, then it has created two distinct `.nax-wt` directories and removed both before returning.
When `persistBakeoffResult` receives a feature result and output directory, then it writes `bakeoff.json` under `bakeoff/<feature>` within that directory.
When results for two features are persisted under one output directory, then both feature-scoped `bakeoff.json` files remain readable and contain their own feature values.

routing.reasoning: Replaces a defective dependency boundary and coordinates config, worktree lifecycle, paths, persistence, and tests.

modifiedFiles.reason: its `withDeps` helper mutates the shared `_contestantDeps` object and its stubs implement `pipeline` as `(config) => …`. This story deletes that default and changes the pipeline parameter to a `ContestantRunContext`, so every test in the file fails against a correct implementation. US-002 owns rewriting them to pass deps explicitly into `runContestant` and to assert on the context object's fields.
supplies a `runContestant` dep typed against the old `(agent, options)` shape. US-002 owns updating it to the profile/context shape.

the case named "AC5: writes bakeoff.json under outputDir …" asserts the file lands directly under the passed `outputDir`. This story moves it to `bakeoff/<feature>/bakeoff.json`, so the assertion fails against a correct implementation. US-002 owns updating it to the feature-scoped path.

userStories.title: Adapt contestant contexts to real runs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement and export the pipeline adapter that executes a contestant context through `Runner.run()` and normalizes run metrics.

**Motivation** — A throwaway spike established the rest of the chain is sound: wiring only `worktreeManager` reached aggregation, ranking, `bakeoff.json`, report rendering, and the exit code, and a single-contestant run completed end to end inside a worktree.

**Approach** — Author the adapter that turns a `ContestantRunContext` into a real run and maps the result back.

**Interface**
```ts
pipeline: (ctx: ContestantRunContext) => Promise<ContestantPipelineResult>;
```

**Scope** — In: a `src/bakeoff/pipeline-adapter.ts` adapter, `run()` option mapping, metrics loading/fallback, barrel export, and CLI seam coverage. Out: profile resolution and context construction (US-001, US-002); worktree guards (US-004); removal of superseded exports/types (US-005).
acceptanceCriteria: When `handleRunAction` receives two resolvable profiles with a stubbed pipeline adapter, then the adapter is invoked exactly twice.
When the pipeline adapter invokes `run`, then its `workdir` equals the context `worktree`.
When the pipeline adapter invokes `run`, then its `prdPath` is located inside the context `worktree`.
When the pipeline adapter invokes `run`, then its `prdPath` names the context feature.
When the pipeline adapter invokes `run`, then its `statusFile` is located inside the context `outputDir`.
When the pipeline adapter invokes `run`, then its `config` equals the context `config`.
When `run` reports `storiesCompleted`, then the adapter returns a `results` array with that length.
When the pipeline adapter executes a context, then it invokes `loadRunMetrics` with the context `outputDir`.
When `loadRunMetrics` returns story metrics, then the adapter returns one metrics entry per story metric carrying that metric's cost and duration.
When `loadRunMetrics` yields no entries, then the adapter returns one metrics entry derived from the run result `totalCost` and `durationMs`.

routing.reasoning: Introduces a new adapter across runner, hooks, metrics, CLI wiring, and isolated execution context.

userStories.title: Guard bake-off worktrees and committed PRDs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Reserve safe contestant worktree identities, reclaim only stale bake-off branches, and reject uncommitted feature PRDs before spend.

**Motivation** — Feature `prd.json` untracked or carrying uncommitted modifications must reject the whole bake-off before any worktree is created and before any spend.

**Approach** — Contestant worktree ids carry a `bakeoff-` prefix, making `nax/bakeoff-…` a namespace no user branch occupies. Ids are derived from feature and profile, reduced to the character set `validateStoryId` accepts, and truncated to at most 64 characters with a stable distinguishing suffix when the natural id would overflow.

**Scope** — In: safe/truncated ID derivation, reserved-namespace branch reclaim during preflight, committed/clean PRD validation, and per-contestant create-failure reporting. Out: changing `WorktreeManager`'s `hasWorktreeRecord` branch-reclaim guard; reclaiming worktree directories left on disk without a matching git branch; concurrent bake-offs against the same repository; the `nax/bakeoff-` branch namespace is not locked, so two simultaneous bake-offs of the same feature and profile may contend for one worktree; pipeline adapter work (US-003); terminal removal work (US-005).
acceptanceCriteria: When the PRD-tracking guard rejects a compare invocation, then `handleRunAction` creates no worktree.
When a worktree ID is derived for a feature and profile, then it begins with `bakeoff-`.
When a profile name contains characters outside the story-ID alphabet, then its derived worktree ID passes `validateStoryId` without throwing.
When a feature and profile yield an overlong natural ID, then the derived worktree ID is at most 64 characters long.
When two distinct feature-and-profile pairs both yield overlong natural IDs, then their derived worktree IDs differ.
When preflight finds a leftover `nax/bakeoff-<id>` branch with no worktree record, then it removes that branch and subsequent worktree creation for the ID succeeds.
When preflight runs with a branch not beginning `nax/bakeoff-`, then that branch still exists afterward.
When a feature `prd.json` is untracked by git, then the bake-off rejects with an error naming that PRD path.
When a feature `prd.json` has uncommitted modifications, then the bake-off rejects with an error naming that PRD path.
When the feature PRD is untracked, then the bake-off rejects without invoking the pipeline dependency.
When contestant worktree creation fails, then that contestant is reported with status `dnf-crashed`.

routing.reasoning: Adds git-state safety gates and collision-resistant identity logic across preflight and worktree behavior.

outOfScope: Reclaiming a worktree directory present on disk with no corresponding git branch — the reclaim keys on the branch namespace only.

userStories.title: Remove superseded contestant APIs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Delete obsolete mutable contestant defaults, agent-name validation surface, and old pipeline signature exports.

**Motivation** — Six test files cover this subsystem and all pass, because each test overwrites the production defaults before reading them (`Object.assign(_contestantDeps, overrides)`). The suite validates the algorithm and is structurally blind to the wiring.

**Approach** — Deletion-only. Remove the `_contestantDeps` module-level default and its `src/bakeoff/index.ts` barrel export, the agent-name validation surface superseded by profile resolution, and the superseded `pipeline` signature type. No new code.

**Scope** — In: terminal API cleanup after all profile/context/adapter/guard consumers have migrated, including the compile-time rejection of a stale caller that omits `runContestant` dependencies. Out: new runtime behavior, profile resolution (US-001), context and persistence work (US-002), runner adapter (US-003), and worktree/preflight guards (US-004).
acceptanceCriteria: When `runContestant` is invoked with an explicit deps object providing a worktree manager and a pipeline, then it returns a `ContestantResult` whose `agent` equals the profile name it was given.

routing.reasoning: Mechanical removal of obsolete internal API after all consumers have migrated.
routing.noTestJustification: This is deletion-only cleanup with no new runtime behavior; the migrated behavior is covered by the upstream stories and surviving references are caught by static review and repository quality gates.

analysis: The existing bake-off implementation is an enhancement/refactor, not greenfield. src/bakeoff/preflight.ts:12-93 validates names against KNOWN_AGENT_NAMES and returns unknown-agent; it must resolve each comparison entry with loadProfile(profile, projectRoot), validate the resolved agent.default against ACP_ADAPTER_NAMES and its adapter binary, and retain the existing agents/agent field names as profile labels. src/config/profile.ts:52-100 is the safe, authoritative profile resolver: validateProfileName is private and PROFILE_NOT_FOUND / PROFILE_NAME_INVALID must be handled through loadProfile. src/config/merger.ts:30-123 provides immutable deepMergeConfig semantics, so per-contestant configuration is base config plus one profile overlay, with fallback.enabled pinned false after merging. src/bakeoff/contestant.ts:36-58 declares an unwired _contestantDeps object using unsafe casts; src/bakeoff/contestant.ts:81-149 defaults runContestant to it, converting missing production wiring into dnf-crashed. Replace it with an explicit required dependency and a ContestantRunContext that carries profile, merged config, worktree, outputDir, and feature. The current pipeline only receives config, so it cannot correctly map run options to contestant state. src/bakeoff/coordinator.ts:19-139 runs validated entries sequentially, persists directly under outputDir, and routes CLI compare input; it must construct/profile-thread contestant config and persist under bakeoff/<feature>. Existing CLI tests deliberately assert callArg.agents (test/unit/bakeoff/run-action.test.ts:49-52), so those field names are a compatibility constraint even though values now denote profiles. src/runtime/paths.ts and src/runtime/index.ts establish that the output root must derive from projectOutputDir(projectKey, baseConfig.outputDir), never from a hardcoded global config path; setting the contestant merged config.outputDir is the only available run seam because RunOptions has no outputDir. src/worktree/manager.ts:66-204 validates story IDs and creates nax/<storyId> branches but only reclaims a stale branch when its private hasWorktreeRecord proves prior manager ownership. Bake-off preflight must derive safe, bounded bakeoff- IDs, reclaim only stale nax/bakeoff-* branches, and leave other namespace collisions untouched. src/prd/validate.ts:20-38 supplies the exact story-id grammar. The new pipeline adapter belongs in src/bakeoff/pipeline-adapter.ts, separate from contestant.ts, and maps context to runner.run() plus loadRunMetrics(outputDir), preserving result metrics with a run-result fallback. Existing test coverage is concentrated in test/unit/bakeoff/preflight.test.ts, contestant.test.ts, coordinator.test.ts, report.test.ts, and run-action.test.ts; contestant tests currently mutate _contestantDeps and use the old config-only pipeline signature, so US-002 must replace those helpers. Risks: profile/agent-name collisions make dual interpretation unsafe; deleting default deps changes internal call signatures and exports; output relocation can break report consumers; git branch reclamation must never delete user branches; and untracked or modified PRDs must stop all spend before worktree creation. Migration is intentionally internal: retain BakeoffOptions.agents and ContestantResult.agent names, change only their semantics to profile names, export the adapter through the bakeoff barrel, update unit/integration seams, then remove obsolete agent-name/default-deps API after consumers have moved.
outOfScope: Keeping, merging, or applying a winning contestant's work; the bake-off remains report-only.
Running contestants in parallel; contestants continue to execute sequentially.
Making `nax run --dry-run` free of LLM routing cost.
Copying an uncommitted PRD into a contestant worktree.
Accepting bare agent names as contestants; `--compare` accepts profile names only.
US-002 only: worktree removal failures remain best-effort and do not change the contestant's reported status.
US-004 only: reclaiming worktree directories left on disk without a matching git branch.
Concurrent bake-offs against the same repository; the `nax/bakeoff-` branch namespace is not locked, so two simultaneous bake-offs of the same feature and profile may contend for one worktree.
